meta_title: Troubleshooting VpnHood! MANAGER: Servers, Farms and Keys | VpnHood!
meta_description: Fix what VpnHood! MANAGER shows when something goes wrong: a server that never connects, shows an error or stops reporting, a farm's red message, a key that will not open, and apps that cannot connect.
title: Troubleshooting
lead: When something goes wrong, VpnHood! MANAGER usually shows it first: in a server's status, as a message in red, or as an error when you open a key. Find what you see below, and what to do about it.
status_intro: A server's [manager_status] tells you how it is doing:
st_not_installed: [manager_not_installed]: it has not reached MANAGER yet.
st_configuring: [manager_configuring]: it is taking new settings, which takes a minute or two.
st_working: [manager_idle] or [manager_active]: it works, and is [manager_active] while devices are connected.
st_lost: [manager_lost]: it has stopped reporting to MANAGER.
st_error: [manager_error]: it could not use its settings.
status_new: New connections go only to a server that is [manager_idle], [manager_active] or [manager_configuring].
ssh_desc: When MANAGER cannot install a server over SSH, it shows an error, with everything it got back under [manager_details]. The usual ones:
ssh_no_public: If it says [manager_err_no_public], enter the server's public IP address, or a name that points to it: MANAGER reaches the server over the internet.
ssh_connect: If the connection is refused or times out, MANAGER could not reach SSH on the server: make sure the server accepts SSH from the internet on that port, or install it with a command instead.
ssh_denied: If it says [manager_err_permission_denied], the user name, the password or the key is wrong.
ssh_password: If it says [manager_err_login_password], the user needs its password for sudo: enter it under [manager_ssh_password], even when you sign in with a key.
ssh_failed: If it says [manager_err_install_failed], the installer ran but did not finish, and [manager_details] shows what it printed. The user must be allowed to use sudo, which has to be on the machine even for root.
never_desc: A server stays [manager_not_installed] until it reaches MANAGER, which it does over HTTPS, at [manager_agent_host], a minute or so after its installer finishes. If it stays that way:
never_output: Read what the install command printed. If it stopped with an error, fix that and run the command again: the command works until you delete the server.
never_outbound: Make sure the server can reach [manager_agent_host] over HTTPS: a firewall or a network that blocks it keeps the server out.
never_log: Look in the server's log, which says why it cannot connect: see Start and stop the server, or Start, stop and check the server in Docker.
error_desc: When a server cannot use its settings, its status turns [manager_error], and its page says why, in red, under [manager_error]. It tries again every minute, so the error goes once you remove its cause.
error_tcp: If it says [manager_err_no_tcp], the server could not open any of its TCP ports. Under [manager_access_points], a red icon beside a port marks one it could not open: select it to see why. Most often another program already uses the port. Free the port, or give the access point another one, as in Change an address.
error_version: If it says [manager_err_version], the server is older than MANAGER accepts: run its install command again, which installs the latest version.
error_restart: A server whose settings have failed for a week tries only every half hour. Once you remove the cause, restart it to try at once.
lost_desc: A server reports to MANAGER every few minutes. When it misses several reports in a row, its status turns [manager_lost]: the machine is down, the server has stopped, or it cannot reach [manager_agent_host]. It gets no new connections until it reports again, and the farm's other servers carry on.
lost_fix: Check that the machine is running, then check the server's status and log, and restart it: see Start and stop the server, or Start, stop and check the server in Docker.
farm_title: A farm shows a red message
farm_desc: A red message under a farm's name means MANAGER could not build the farm's token, the part of a key that tells apps how to reach the farm's servers. Until you fix it, the farm keeps its last working token, so its keys carry its old addresses.
farm_self_signed: If it says [manager_err_farm_self_signed], apps could find the farm's servers neither by a trusted domain nor by an address in the keys. Give one of its servers an address whose [manager_mode] is [manager_public_in_token], as in An access point's settings, or give the farm your own domain: see Use your own domain. A new farm shows this until its first server is installed.
farm_domain_only: If it says [manager_err_farm_domain_only], the certificate the keys carry has its [manager_signing] set to [manager_domain_only], which keys cannot carry. Choose another [manager_signing] for it, or put another certificate in the keys: see The certificate in the keys.
key_desc: If [manager_access_key] on a key's page says [manager_err_token_not_ready], the key's farm has never had a working token. Open the farm and fix its red message, as above, and the key opens.
apps_intro: When a device cannot connect, the app says why:
apps_key: If it says the key has expired, is locked or has used up its traffic, open the key in MANAGER: a key stops working once it expires, uses up its traffic or is turned off.
apps_no_server: If it says no server is available, none of the farm's servers can take a new connection: check their status, as above.
apps_unreachable: If it cannot reach the server, check that the addresses whose [manager_mode] is [manager_public_in_token] are your servers' public ones, and that the server's firewall, or your cloud's, lets in their TCP port. If it connects on some networks but not on others, those networks block the server: see Keep your server's IP address from being blocked.
next_domain: Use your own domain with a trusted certificate
next_blocking: Keep your server's IP address from being blocked
